records.source: Σὺ οὖν, τέκνον μου, ἐνδυναμοῦ ἐν τῇ χάριτι τῇ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ ἃ ἤκουσας παρ’ ἐμοῦ διὰ πολλῶν μαρτύρων, ταῦτα παράθου πιστοῖς ἀνθρώποις, οἵτινες ἱκανοὶ ἔσονται καὶ ἑτέρους διδάξαι.
records.gloss: You therefore, child of me, be strengthened in the grace the [one] in Christ Jesus, \v 2 and what you heard from me through many witnesses, these entrust to faithful men, who able will be also others to teach.
pieces: So you, my son, be strong in the grace that is in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.
And what you heard from me before many witnesses, pass on to trustworthy people who will be able to teach others as well.

L.1: You then, my child, be strengthened by the grace that is in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus,
L.2: and what you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses, entrust these things to faithful {{gender:people|men}}, who will be able to teach others also.

R.1: So, my son, let the grace of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus make you strong.
R.2: You heard my teaching, and many other people heard it too. Now teach it to people you can trust, people who will be able to teach others.

decisions.choice: through many witnesses: in the presence of many witnesses
alternatives: through the mediation of many witnesses
decisions.reason: διὰ here most likely means "in the presence of": Paul's teaching was public and confirmed by many.

decisions.choice: a chain of teaching: Paul, Timothy, faithful people, others
decisions.reason: The verb παράθου is the verb of "deposit" (1:14): the gospel is entrusted from one to another.
ἀνθρώποις is the general word for human beings.
Title setting.
The word means human beings in general (m3); Balanced and Readable say "people".
As in 1:2.

records.heading: A good soldier of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus

records.source: συγκακοπάθησον ὡς καλὸς στρατιώτης Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
records.gloss: Share in suffering as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
pieces: Join with me in suffering, like a good soldier of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

L.3: Share in suffering as a good soldier of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus.

R.3: Suffer with me, like a good soldier who serves {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

decisions.reason: The first of three pictures (soldier, athlete, farmer, verses 3-6): each works hard and looks to a reward.
Title setting.

records.source: οὐδεὶς στρατευόμενος ἐμπλέκεται ταῖς τοῦ βίου πραγματείαις, ἵνα τῷ στρατολογήσαντι ἀρέσῃ·
records.gloss: No one serving as a soldier entangles himself in the of life affairs, so that the [one] having enlisted [him] he may please;
pieces: No soldier on active duty gets tangled up in civilian affairs; he wants to please the officer who enlisted him.

L.4: No one serving as a soldier gets entangled in the affairs of everyday life, so that he may please the one who enlisted him.

R.4: A soldier does not get busy with other things in life. He wants to please his commanding officer.

decisions.reason: Roman soldiers on service were not to engage in trade or farming; their duty was to their commander.

records.source: ἐὰν δὲ καὶ ἀθλῇ τις, οὐ στεφανοῦται ἐὰν μὴ νομίμως ἀθλήσῃ·
records.gloss: If and also competes anyone, not he is crowned unless lawfully he competes;
pieces: In the same way, an athlete does not receive the winner's crown unless he competes by the rules.

L.5: Also, if anyone competes as an athlete, he is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules.

R.5: An athlete does not win the prize unless he obeys the rules of the game.

decisions.reason: In the games the winner received a wreath; athletes had to keep the rules, including training, to qualify (1 Corinthians 9:24-27).

records.source: τὸν κοπιῶντα γεωργὸν δεῖ πρῶτον τῶν καρπῶν μεταλαμβάνειν.
records.gloss: The laboring farmer it is necessary first of the fruits to share.
pieces: The farmer who does the hard work should be the first to eat from the harvest.

L.6: The hardworking farmer ought to be the first to share in the crops.

R.6: A farmer who works hard should be the first to eat some of the food he grows.

decisions.choice: the hardworking farmer shares first in the crops
decisions.reason: Hard work brings its reward. Paul uses the same picture for the support of those who work in the gospel (1 Corinthians 9:7, 9:10).

records.source: νόει ὃ λέγω· δώσει γάρ σοι ὁ κύριος σύνεσιν ἐν πᾶσιν.
records.gloss: Consider what I say; will give for to you the Lord understanding in all things.
pieces: Reflect on what I am saying, for the Lord will give you understanding in all things.

L.7: Think about what I am saying, for the Lord will give you understanding in everything.

R.7: Think about what I am telling you. The Lord will help you understand everything.

decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read the wish "may the Lord give". The SBLGNT has the future "will give".

records.source: Μνημόνευε Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐγηγερμένον ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυίδ, κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιόν μου·
records.gloss: Remember Jesus Christ having been raised from [the] dead, of [the] seed of David, according to the gospel of me;
pieces: Remember Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, raised from the dead and descended from David, as my gospel proclaims.

L.8: Remember Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, raised from the dead, a descendant of David, according to my gospel.

R.8: Remember Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. God raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the dead, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was born into King David's family. That is the good news I tell people.

decisions.choice: raised from the dead: the perfect, raised and still living
decisions.reason: ἐγηγερμένον is perfect: Christ was raised and remains alive.

decisions.choice: of the seed of David: the promised king
decisions.reason: God promised David a descendant who would reign for ever (2 Samuel 7:12-16; Romans 1:3).

decisions.choice: my gospel: the gospel I preach
decisions.reason: Not a different gospel, but the one entrusted to Paul (Romans 2:16).
Title setting.

records.heading: God's word is not chained

records.source: ἐν ᾧ κακοπαθῶ μέχρι δεσμῶν ὡς κακοῦργος.
records.gloss: for which I suffer hardship to the point of chains as a criminal.
pieces: For this gospel I am suffering, even to the point of being chained like a criminal.

L.9: For [this gospel] I suffer hardship, even to the point of being chained like a criminal.

R.9: Because of this good news I am suffering. I am even chained up in prison, as if I were a criminal.

decisions.reason: κακοῦργος is a wrongdoer, the word used of the criminals crucified with Jesus (Luke 23:32-33).

records.source: ἀλλὰ ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ οὐ δέδεται·
records.gloss: but the word of the God not has been bound;
pieces: But God's word is not chained.

L.9: But the word of God is not chained.

R.9: But no one can chain up God's message.

decisions.choice: the word of God is not chained
decisions.reason: δέδεται is the verb for binding Paul: the messenger is bound, but the message goes on (Philippians 1:12-14).

records.source: διὰ τοῦτο πάντα ὑπομένω διὰ τοὺς ἐκλεκτούς, ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ σωτηρίας τύχωσιν τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ μετὰ δόξης αἰωνίου.
records.gloss: Because of this all things I endure because of the chosen, so that also they salvation may obtain the [one] in Christ Jesus with glory eternal.
pieces: So I endure everything for the sake of God's chosen people, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, and with it eternal glory.

L.10: Therefore I endure everything for the sake of the chosen, so that they also may obtain the salvation that is in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, with eternal glory.

R.10: So I am willing to go through anything for the people God has chosen. I want them to be saved by {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus and to share in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eternal glory.

decisions.choice: the chosen: God's people, including those not yet believing
decisions.reason: ἐκλεκτούς are those God has chosen (Titus 1:1). Paul endures so that they may come to salvation.
Title setting.

records.source: πιστὸς ὁ λόγος· εἰ γὰρ συναπεθάνομεν, καὶ συζήσομεν·
records.gloss: Trustworthy [is] the saying: if for we died with [him], also we will live with [him];
pieces: Here is a saying you can rely on: If we died with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, we will also live with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.11: The saying [is] trustworthy: For if we died with [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], we will also live with [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}].

R.11: Here is something true: If we died with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, we will also live with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: a trustworthy saying: perhaps an early hymn
decisions.reason: Verses 11-13 have four balanced "if" lines, like a hymn or confession the churches knew.

decisions.choice: if we died with him: in baptism and faith
decisions.reason: Believers share Christ's death and so his life (Romans 6:3-8).
The compound verbs ("die with", "live with") imply "him".
Readable names Christ.

records.source: εἰ ὑπομένομεν, καὶ συμβασιλεύσομεν· εἰ ἀρνησόμεθα, κἀκεῖνος ἀρνήσεται ἡμᾶς·
records.gloss: if we endure, also we will reign with [him]; if we will deny, also that one will deny us;
pieces: If we endure, we will also reign with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. If we deny {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will also deny us.

L.12: If we endure, we will also reign with [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}]; if we deny [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also will deny us.

R.12: If we keep going when we suffer, we will rule with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. If we say we do not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will say that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not know us.

decisions.choice: if we deny him, he will deny us: the words of Jesus
decisions.reason: "Whoever denies me before others, I will also deny before my Father in heaven" (Matthew 10:33).

records.source: εἰ ἀπιστοῦμεν, ἐκεῖνος πιστὸς μένει· ἀρνήσασθαι ἑαυτὸν οὐ δύναται.
records.gloss: if we are faithless, that one faithful remains; to deny himself not he is able.
pieces: If we are unfaithful, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remains faithful, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cannot be false to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.

L.13: If we are faithless, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remains faithful, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cannot deny {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.

R.13: If we are not faithful, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is still faithful, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cannot go against who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is.

decisions.choice: if we are faithless, he remains faithful
alternatives: a warning: he will be faithful to his word to judge
decisions.reason: The fourth line breaks the pattern: Christ's faithfulness does not depend on ours. Most read it as assurance; some as a warning that he stays true to his word, including verse 12. Either way he "cannot deny himself".
ἀπιστέω means to be unfaithful or not to believe.

records.source: Ταῦτα ὑπομίμνῃσκε, διαμαρτυρόμενος ἐνώπιον τοῦ κυρίου, μὴ λογομαχεῖν, ἐπ’ οὐδὲν χρήσιμον, ἐπὶ καταστροφῇ τῶν ἀκουόντων.
records.gloss: These things remind [them], charging before the Lord not to fight about words, for nothing useful, to the ruin of those hearing.
pieces: Keep reminding people of these things, and warn them before the Lord not to quarrel about words. It does no good and only ruins those who listen.

L.14: Remind [them] of these things, solemnly charging [them] before the Lord not to quarrel about words, which is of no use and ruins those who listen.

R.14: Keep reminding the believers of these things. Warn them, in front of the Lord, not to argue about words. Arguments like that do no good. They only hurt the people who listen.

decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "God".
καταστροφῇ is overturning, the root of "catastrophe".

records.heading: A worker approved by God

records.source: σπούδασον σεαυτὸν δόκιμον παραστῆσαι τῷ θεῷ, ἐργάτην ἀνεπαίσχυντον, ὀρθοτομοῦντα τὸν λόγον τῆς ἀληθείας.
records.gloss: Be eager yourself approved to present to the God, a worker not ashamed, rightly cutting the word of the truth.
pieces: Make every effort to stand before God tested and approved, a worker with nothing to be ashamed of, who handles the message of truth correctly.

L.15: Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved, a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly handling the word of truth.

R.15: Work hard so that God will be pleased with you. Be a worker who does not need to be ashamed, and teach God's true message the right way.

decisions.choice: do your best: be eager, make every effort
decisions.reason: σπουδάζω is to hurry, to be eager.
ὀρθοτομέω means to cut straight, as a road is cut straight or a stonemason cuts true. Timothy is to teach the word without twisting it.
"Message" is plainer than "word" here; the key term "truth" stays.

records.source: τὰς δὲ βεβήλους κενοφωνίας περιΐστασο· ἐπὶ πλεῖον γὰρ προκόψουσιν ἀσεβείας, καὶ ὁ λόγος αὐτῶν ὡς γάγγραινα νομὴν ἕξει· ὧν ἐστιν Ὑμέναιος καὶ Φίλητος, οἵτινες περὶ τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἠστόχησαν, λέγοντες ἀνάστασιν ἤδη γεγονέναι, καὶ ἀνατρέπουσιν τήν τινων πίστιν.
records.gloss: The but profane empty chatter avoid; to more for they will advance of ungodliness, \v 17 and the word of them like gangrene pasture will have; of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus, \v 18 who concerning the truth have missed the mark, saying [the] resurrection already to have happened, and they overturn the of some faith.
pieces: Stay away from godless, empty chatter, because those who indulge in it will become more and more ungodly,
and their teaching will spread like gangrene. Hymenaeus and Philetus are among them.
They have wandered away from the truth, saying that the resurrection has already taken place, and they are destroying the faith of some.

L.16: But avoid irreverent, empty chatter, for they will go on to more ungodliness,
L.17: and their talk will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
L.18: who have swerved from the truth, saying that the resurrection has already happened, and they are overturning the faith of some.

R.16: Stay away from people who talk about foolish things that have nothing to do with God. That kind of talk makes people turn further away from God.
R.17: Their teaching spreads like a disease that eats away the body. Hymenaeus and Philetus are two of these people.
R.18: They have turned away from the truth. They say that the dead have already been raised to new life. They are destroying some people's faith.

decisions.choice: they will advance: those who talk this way
decisions.reason: προκόψουσιν is plural and most naturally refers to the people who engage in it.
γάγγραινα is a spreading sore that eats away healthy flesh; it is set against "sound" (healthy) teaching (1:13).
They taught that the resurrection was only a present spiritual reality, denying a future bodily resurrection (compare 1 Corinthians 15:12). Hymenaeus is probably the man of 1 Timothy 1:20.

records.source: ὁ μέντοι στερεὸς θεμέλιος τοῦ θεοῦ ἕστηκεν, ἔχων τὴν σφραγῖδα ταύτην· Ἔγνω κύριος τοὺς ὄντας αὐτοῦ, καί· Ἀποστήτω ἀπὸ ἀδικίας πᾶς ὁ ὀνομάζων τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου.
records.gloss: The nevertheless firm foundation of the God stands, having the seal this: Knew [the] Lord those being his, and: Let depart from unrighteousness everyone naming the name of [the] Lord.
pieces: But God's solid foundation stands firm, sealed with these words: "The Lord knows those who are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}," and "Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from wickedness."

L.19: Nevertheless, God's firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: "[The] Lord knows those who are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}," and, "Let everyone who names the name of [the] Lord depart from unrighteousness."

R.19: But what God has built stands strong, like a building on a solid foundation. It is marked with these words: "The Lord knows who belongs to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}," and "Everyone who says they belong to the Lord must stop doing wrong."

decisions.choice: the Lord knows those who are his: Numbers 16:5
decisions.reason: When Korah rebelled, Moses said, "The LORD will show who is his" (Numbers 16:5, in its Greek form). God knows his own, whatever false teachers claim.

decisions.choice: let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from unrighteousness
decisions.reason: The words echo Numbers 16:26 ("depart from the tents of these wicked men") and Isaiah 26:13 and 52:11. Belonging to the Lord means leaving evil.

decisions.choice: seal: an inscription on a foundation stone
decisions.reason: Foundation stones sometimes bore inscriptions; a seal also marked ownership. God's foundation, his church or his truth, bears two marks.

records.source: Ἐν μεγάλῃ δὲ οἰκίᾳ οὐκ ἔστιν μόνον σκεύη χρυσᾶ καὶ ἀργυρᾶ ἀλλὰ καὶ ξύλινα καὶ ὀστράκινα, καὶ ἃ μὲν εἰς τιμὴν ἃ δὲ εἰς ἀτιμίαν·
records.gloss: In a great but house not there are only vessels gold and silver but also wooden and earthen, and some for honor, some but for dishonor;
pieces: In a large house there are not only gold and silver dishes but also wooden and clay ones, some for special occasions and some for common use.

L.20: Now in a large house there are not only vessels of gold and silver but also of wood and clay, some for honorable use and some for dishonorable.

R.20: A big house has dishes made of gold and silver, but it also has dishes made of wood and clay. Some are used for special purposes, and some are used for ordinary things.

decisions.choice: vessels for honor and for dishonor: the household picture
decisions.reason: σκεύη is a container or utensil. In a great house some are for fine use and some for common or dirty use. The picture leads to verse 21.

records.heading: Vessels for special use

records.source: ἐὰν οὖν τις ἐκκαθάρῃ ἑαυτὸν ἀπὸ τούτων, ἔσται σκεῦος εἰς τιμήν, ἡγιασμένον, εὔχρηστον τῷ δεσπότῃ, εἰς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἡτοιμασμένον.
records.gloss: If therefore anyone cleanses himself from these, he will be a vessel for honor, having been sanctified, useful to the master, for every work good having been prepared.
pieces: Those who keep themselves clean from such things will be vessels for special use, made holy, useful to the master, and ready for every good work.

L.21: So if anyone cleanses himself from these things, he will be a vessel for honor, set apart as holy, useful to the master, prepared for every good work.

R.21: If you keep yourself pure from these bad things, you will be like a dish used for special purposes. You will be holy and useful to your Master, ready to do every kind of good work.

decisions.choice: from these: from the dishonorable vessels, the false teachers and their ways
decisions.reason: τούτων most likely refers back to the "vessels for dishonor" and to the false teaching of verses 16-18.

decisions.choice: the master: the owner of the house, God
decisions.reason: δεσπότῃ is the master of the house; in the picture, the Lord.
The Greek "anyone" includes women; Balanced and Readable avoid "himself".

records.source: τὰς δὲ νεωτερικὰς ἐπιθυμίας φεῦγε, δίωκε δὲ δικαιοσύνην, πίστιν, ἀγάπην, εἰρήνην μετὰ τῶν ἐπικαλουμένων τὸν κύριον ἐκ καθαρᾶς καρδίας.
records.gloss: The but youthful desires flee, pursue but righteousness, faith, love, peace with those calling on the Lord out of a pure heart.
pieces: Run away from the passions of youth, and pursue righteousness, faith, love and peace, together with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.

L.22: So flee youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love [and] peace, along with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.

R.22: Run away from the wrong desires that young people often have. Instead, try hard to live a righteous life, and to have faith, love and peace. Do this together with people who pray to the Lord with pure hearts.

decisions.choice: youthful passions: the desires of youth
decisions.reason: νεωτερικὰς covers not only sexual desire but impatience, love of argument and ambition, which fit the context (verse 23).

decisions.choice: those who call on the Lord: believers
decisions.reason: A biblical phrase for God's people (Joel 2:32; Romans 10:13).

records.source: τὰς δὲ μωρὰς καὶ ἀπαιδεύτους ζητήσεις παραιτοῦ, εἰδὼς ὅτι γεννῶσι μάχας·
records.gloss: The but foolish and ignorant controversies refuse, knowing that they produce quarrels;
pieces: Have nothing to do with foolish and ignorant arguments; you know they only lead to quarrels.

L.23: Refuse foolish and ignorant controversies, knowing that they breed quarrels.

R.23: Stay away from foolish and stupid arguments. You know that they only start fights.

decisions.reason: ἀπαιδεύτους is untrained, unschooled: arguments with no grounding in sound teaching.

records.source: δοῦλον δὲ κυρίου οὐ δεῖ μάχεσθαι, ἀλλὰ ἤπιον εἶναι πρὸς πάντας, διδακτικόν, ἀνεξίκακον, ἐν πραΰτητι παιδεύοντα τοὺς ἀντιδιατιθεμένους, μήποτε δώῃ αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς μετάνοιαν εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας, καὶ ἀνανήψωσιν ἐκ τῆς τοῦ διαβόλου παγίδος, ἐζωγρημένοι ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ ἐκείνου θέλημα.
records.gloss: A slave but of [the] Lord not must quarrel, but gentle be toward all, able to teach, patient under wrong, \v 25 in gentleness correcting those opposing, if perhaps may give them the God repentance unto knowledge of truth, \v 26 and they may come to their senses out of the of the devil snare, having been captured by him for the of that one will.
pieces: The Lord's servant must not be quarrelsome but kind to everyone, able to teach and patient with difficult people,
gently correcting those who oppose him. Perhaps God will grant them repentance and they will come to know the truth,
and come to their senses and escape the trap of the devil, who has held them captive to do his will.

L.24: And the Lord's slave must not quarrel, but be gentle toward all, able to teach, patient when wronged,
L.25: correcting opponents with gentleness. Perhaps God may grant them repentance leading to knowledge of [the] truth,
L.26: and they may come to their senses [and escape] from the snare of the devil, having been captured by him to do his will.

R.24: A servant of the Lord must not fight. They must be kind to everyone, able to teach, and patient when people treat them badly.
R.25: They must gently correct people who are against them. Maybe God will help those people turn away from their sins and know the truth.
R.26: Then they will think clearly again. They will escape from the devil's trap, the trap he used to catch them so that they would do what he wants.

decisions.choice: the Lord's slave: one who belongs to the Lord and serves him
decisions.reason: δοῦλον is the word for a slave, a title Paul uses of himself (Titus 1:1; Philippians 1:1).

decisions.choice: captured by him to do his will: by the devil, for the devil's will
alternatives: captured by the Lord's slave, to do God's will
captured by the devil, and now to do God's will
decisions.reason: Two different pronouns are used, αὐτοῦ ("him") and ἐκείνου ("that one"), which may refer to different persons. Most naturally both refer to the devil, just named; but ἐκείνου may point back to God (verse 25), so that they escape the devil to do God's will, or αὐτοῦ to the Lord's slave who wins them back.
Repentance is God's gift; the teacher's part is gentle correction.
"Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".
Readable uses "they", since any of the Lord's servants is meant.
